estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.classification_evidence: Own-model pick stability: single-fit pairwise flip rate (two individual bootstrap-refit draws disagreeing) 26.4% vs bagged split-half flip rate (mean of first 60 vs mean of second 60 of 120 refit draws disagreeing) 4.5% -- a 5.9x reduction, on 8,933 CFB games / 13 seasons. Accuracy: single-fit 51.14% vs bagged 51.31% (+0.17 pts, bagging beats the single fit). Bagged-vs-baseline (full-vs-thin) paired comparison: -0.168 acc pts [naive interval], P+ 0.383 (up from the single-fit arm's -0.336 pts / P+ 0.262 -- still crosses zero, so unresolved, but a genuine partial improvement in both estimate and P+ relative to not bagging). A DIRECT synthetic falsification attempt (fresh-bootstrap-of-a-training-resample own-model-instability design) found a null result instead (single flip 9.5% vs bagged 10.0%); diagnosed as a comparator design flaw (bootstrapping a bootstrap resample compounds variance rather than testing a fair 'fresh draw of history'), not evidence against the real-data finding. The real-data split-half design (splitting one clean bootstrap ensemble in half, no nested resampling) is the trustworthy comparator.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.description: Average predicted centres over training-row bootstrap-refit draws (bagging) instead of reporting a single point-estimate fit. Screened on the CFB thin-vs-full candidate comparison, reusing the refit draws already computed for the honest interval -- no extra fitting.
estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.notes: The flip-rate reduction (pick stability) is the strong, decisive part of this result; the accuracy/P+ improvement is real but modest and does not clear any promotion bar on its own. Recommend bagging as a default variance-reduction step for FUTURE candidate screens (it cannot move any current pick since it is not wired into any production path), not as a standalone accuracy claim. CORRECTION (recording agent, 2026-08-18): the drafted payload this entry is sourced from recorded effect=+0.17, which is sign-inconsistent with its own probability_positive=0.3825 and its own classification_evidence text ('-0.168 acc pts ... P+ 0.383'); +0.17 was actually the SEPARATE bagged-vs-single-fit accuracy delta (51.31% vs 51.14%), not the bagged-vs-baseline comparison this P+ describes. Recorded here as effect=-0.168 to match docs/estimation_variance.md sec 4a's literal 'Bagged vs. baseline, naive interval | -0.17 pts [naive], P+ 0.383' under this registry's positive-favours-candidate convention. The underlying finding (bagging helps, relative to the single fit) is unchanged by this correction; only the sign of the recorded full-vs-thin effect number is fixed.

estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.classification_evidence: Non-monotonic and noisy: shrink_fraction=1.0 (production strength) gives -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.255; 0.75 -> -0.448 pts P+ 0.181; 0.5 -> -0.414 pts P+ 0.208; 0.25 -> +0.034 pts P+ 0.543 (essentially zero, not a real flip, just the least-negative point); 0.0 -> -1.209 pts P+ 0.041. A matched synthetic check (linear DGP, location-biased residual sample, 100 replicates x n_boot=50) found the OPPOSITE, clean, monotonic pattern instead: shrink=1.0 always best (+1.67 pts, P+ 0.707), declining smoothly to shrink=0 (-5.52 pts, P+ 0.091). Flip-rate DOES fall monotonically with shrinkage in both the real and synthetic data (confirms the mechanism -- production's cover probability threshold is fixed against a nonzero-location residual sample, so uniform positive scaling is NOT sign-invariant, unlike coefficient scaling closed by MOD-06), but the real-data accuracy/P+ sweep does not replicate the synthetic monotonic decline, so there is no basis to claim a shrinkage sweet spot exists.

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.classification_evidence: Ungated (tau=0): -0.336 acc pts, P+ 0.264 (candidate LOSES to baseline). Gated at tau=0.05 (defer to baseline wherever the two arms' cover probabilities differ by <5 points): +0.246 acc pts, P+ 0.9505, f falls 19.8% -> 2.06% (MDE80 1.32 -> 0.43 pts). The sign flip and P+ jump REPLICATE independently on two disjoint season halves built by alternating clean-core seasons (scripts/estvar_f_lever_splithalf.py): half A (2012/14/16/18/21/23/25) P+ 0.399 -> 0.935 at tau 0->0.05; half B (2013/15/17/19/22/24) P+ 0.241 -> 0.744 at tau 0->0.05. Recorded unresolved rather than resolved because tau=0.05 was chosen from a 9-point sweep AFTER seeing the pooled result -- the split-half check supports the QUALITATIVE pattern (a modest disagreement gate makes this comparison provable) but not the specific tau or P+ figure at full precision; a predeclared tau on a train/validation split, confirmed once on a held-out test split, is required before this could be called resolved.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.description: Gate the 'full' CFB feature profile's influence to games where its predicted cover probability disagrees with the 'thin' (market+context+experience only) baseline by at least tau, deferring to the baseline elsewhere. Tests the general 'f lever' principle (MDE80 = 280*sqrt(f/n)): a surgical candidate that only moves the picks it has real information about is more provable than one that perturbs every pick.
estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.notes: This is a DETECTION-METHOD finding, not a new predictive feature -- 'full' and 'thin' are both already-existing profiles. The actionable implication is a general design principle for evaluating future candidates (gate influence to where the candidate disagrees with a simpler baseline), not a pick change. Do not promote or apply to any live model; this only screens the evaluator's own sensitivity. Recorded 2026-08-18 by a recording agent from docs/estimation_variance.md sec 5/sec 6 (the drafting session was barred from writing registry/*.json; this session verified the doc's tau=0.05 row and split-half table before recording, no fields required derivation).

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.classification_evidence: Out-of-screen population (thin_2006_2011 minus 2006-2007, which fall below the 500-game training floor entirely under annual-refit cadence, + regime_2020): 2,533 games, 72 blocks. Real gate (tau=0.05, frozen, not re-swept): -0.316 acc pts, honest 95% interval [-1.323, +0.699] (refit_aware_interval, samples=20000), honest P+ 0.2733 -- crosses zero, does NOT directionally replicate clean-core's positive lean (P+ 0.9505 pooled, 0.935/0.744 split-half). Required placebo control (random gate, same n=411 membership count, seed 20260818): -0.553 acc pts, P+ 0.0512 -- worse than the real gate, which is evidence the disagreement selection is not arbitrary even though neither arm beats baseline here. Gate-membership reliability (120 paired refit draws): 23.09% overall flip rate under training-row resampling (1 - flip rate = 0.7691 recorded as reliability, converted to the registry's higher-is-better convention), 32.82% among point-fit in-gate games, 21.20% among out-gate games -- real instability, not enough alone to close as no_split_half_reliability. Realized f (7.03%) and membership rate (16.23%) are far above clean-core's ~2%, consistent with the flagged sparser-market regime confound (2a caveat 2) and not separable from it in this design. MDE80 at realized f/n is 1.47 pts, worse than the design's own 0.69-pt a-priori estimate and ~6x the original screen's +0.246-pt effect -- underpowered as expected, and the honest read is directional, not resolving, and leans negative rather than positive.

injury_value_lost_gradient.classification_evidence: Unchanged headline: the disagreement statistic resolves (rank-biserial +0.248 [+0.046,+0.450], p=0.016) but the ACCURACY effect does not (+1.75 [-0.69,+4.27], P+ 0.899) on the already-spent [2020, 2021] window, 456 games. NEW this session (docs/injury_value_lost.md): (1) split-half reliability of the underlying value-lost signal, measured on the full 2009-2025 history (4,431 games, 384 team-seasons, temporal odd/even-week split) is Pearson r=0.874 [0.843,0.901], Spearman-Brown corrected full-length reliability=0.933 [0.915,0.948], P+=1.000 (4000/4000 bootstrap draws) -- rules out 'refuted: no split-half reliability' per AGENTS.md. (2) The RAPM-participation value-lost construct (M6, the family's one same-kind negative, -0.43 pts) has EQUALLY high reliability (0.860 raw / 0.925 corrected) -- so reliability does NOT explain M6's negative sign; more likely M6 tests the marginal value of a second, QB-inclusive, correlated value-lost construct stacked on top of one already in the model (full_player_participation = full_player_value + participation family), not whether value-lost as a concept works. (3) The mechanism-screen result survives a market-line-movement control unchanged (value_magnitude vs |close-open| line move: Pearson 0.029, near-zero; residualized disagreement rank-biserial 0.249 [0.047,0.451] p=0.016, statistically identical to the raw 0.248). (4) Survives dropping every QB-involved game: on the 397/456 games (87%) where neither presumed starter carried any listed injury, rank-biserial is still positive (+0.188 [-0.027,0.403], p=0.086) at comparable magnitude to the full sample -- consistent with the structural code finding that injury_skill_epa_value_lost deliberately zeroes QB rushing/receiving production (players.py:1260-1283), so this is provably not a QB proxy. (5) A methodologically CLEANER isolation exists and was run for the first time: player_value profile on game_features_player_value.parquet (built with FIXED-prior severity per its manifest player_feature_version=v2 tag, confirmed NOT learned) contrasted against the player baseline differs by ONLY the two value-lost columns -- zero semantics-shift confound, unlike this entry's original B-A contrast which mixed learned-severity semantics_shift into the same delta. That clean contrast gives +1.316 pts [-0.460,+3.247], P+ 0.8875, on the same 456 games, 26 disagreements (61.5% candidate win rate) -- smaller than +1.75 (removing the confound costs about a third of a point) but directionally intact. Recommend citing +1.316/P+0.8875 as the number to predeclare a narrowed family against, not the conflated +1.75 recorded here.
